headline: Approved $521,064 preschool grant, $236,835.00 PRISM literacy grant, and $27,831.00 computer science grant; rejected flag display policy petition.
summary: Approved a consent agenda with donations and personnel items, four grants, a new policy on interacting with law enforcement officers, and 2026-2027 second meal prices. Rejected a petition on flag displays on school grounds, and a motion to reconsider it failed 2-6. Referred three items to Operations and Governance and held a district boundary and realignment report.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including donations and personnel items, 8-0.
Rejected and filed petition c&p 6-14 on displaying flags on school grounds, 8-0.
Motion to consider reconsideration of petition c&p 6-14 failed, 2-6.
Approved and filed the superintendent's Welcome Back report, 6-0 by voice vote.
Held gb 6-72 on the district boundary and realignment report, 3-0.
Approved the Operations and Governance items as presented, 6-0 by voice vote.
Approved the Commonwealth Preschool Partnership Initiative grant of $521,064, the High Dosage Tutoring Grant, the PRISM grant of $236,835.00, and the Computer Science Engage Grant of $27,831.00, 6-0.
Approved and filed gb 6-94 recognizing June and September as Pride Months, 6-0.
Referred gb 6-95, an update to Policy JCA on assignment of students to schools, to Operations and Governance, 6-0.
Referred c&p 6-6 on the district voluntary transfer policy to Operations and Governance, 6-0.
Referred gb 6-96 on policies ECAF, IHBG, and JFBB to Operations and Governance, 6-0.
Approved new policy ACL, Interaction with Law Enforcement Officers, and filed the item, 6-0.
Approved the second meal prices for 2026-2027, 6-0.

J.  Public Petition  
 c&p 6-14 (Michael Douglas) 
   (September 3, 2026) 
For the Worcester School Committee to establish a formal district policy governing 
the display of flags on school grounds and within municipally controlled public school 
buildings. Specifically, I request that the School Committee enact a policy to prohibit 
the flying or displaying of any flag on public school premises that is not an official 
governmental banner or recognized military/veteran remembrance banner, restricted 
exclusively to: 
1.        The national flag of the United States of America 
2.        The official flag of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts 
3.        The official flag of the City of Worcester 
4.        The official National League of Families POW/MIA flag  
 
EXCEPTIONS CLAUSE: 
This policy shall not apply to flags or banners used temporarily for direct classroom 
instruction (including, but not limited to, world history, geography, or foreign 
language classes), official school sports and spirit flags, or recognized U.S. military 
branch flags. 
 
REASON FOR PETITION: 
To establish symbolic uniformity, reduce community division, and ensure that public 
school infrastructure remains focused exclusively on core civic symbols and 
educational neutrality. 
  
 Michael Douglas, of Worcester, presented his public petition to the Committee. 
  
Member Biancheria noted that this petition is a request to the School Committee and 
it is rare to immediately file a petition. She noted different celebrations take place in 
WPS and she will be making a list of celebrations that occur. She noted concern that 
filing this petition is limited and not all inclusive and WPS should be able to look at 
additional ways to express those celebrations.  
 
A motion was made. A “yes” vote would support and refer this petition to 
Operations and Governance. A “no” vote would reject and file this petition. 
On a roll call vote: Member Alvarez, no; Member Biancheria, no; Member 
Binienda, no; Member Guardiola, no; Member Johnson, no; Member Mailman, 
no; Vice Chair McCullough, no; Mayor Petty, no. By a margin of 8-0, the 
petition was rejected and filed.  
 
A motion was made to consider reconsideration. On a roll call vote: Member 
Alvarez no; Member Biancheria, yes; Member Binienda, yes; Member 
Guardiola, no; Member Johnson, no; Member Mailman, no; Vice Chair 
McCullough, no; Mayor Petty, no. By a margin of 2-6, the motion failed.

 ros 6-11 (Administration)

   (September 3, 2026) 
 Welcome Back - Opening of Schools  
 
Superintendent Allen presented his report. More than 24,000 students (primary 
enrollment numbers, official numbers will be released in October) started the 
2026-2027 school year. The Mayor and several School Committee members, and 
several media outlets attended Flagg Street School on August 31, 2026, to welcome 
students.  
 
The annual leadership convening took place at Doherty Memorial High School. The 
soft launch of Stand Against Racism also took place at this event in conjunction with 
the YMCA. The official launch will be announced soon.  
 
Superintendent Allen reviewed the members of his cabinet and noted that it has 
expanded to include the Director of Special Education, Director of Compliance and 
School Improvement, Director of Multilingual Education, Director of Research and 
Accountability, Director of Teaching and Learning, Director of Access, Equity, and 
Opportunity, Director of College and Career Readiness, and Director of Student 
Supports and Engagement.  
 
Facilities, nutrition, transportation, and school safety departments worked busily over 
the summer and were prepared to welcome all students back this week.  
 
Human Resources hired a total of 246 new staffers, with 144 teachers and 48 
paraprofessionals included in this count. Superintendent Allen announced the names 
of newly appointed/hired Principals, Assistant Principals, Deans, and Focused 
Instructional Coaches. 
 
Member Mailman clarified that the Stand Against Racism program is not just for 
sports. Superintendent Allen confirmed that this program will be present in both  
athletics and at the school level.  
  
A motion was made to approve and file this report. On a voice vote of 6-0, 
the motion was approved. Member Biancheria, Member Roy and Mayor Petty 
were absent for the vote.

 (February 26, 2026)

Results: On a 3-0 vote, these items were filed.  
 
Member Binienda clarified with Nick Stellitano of Dillinger Associates that once all 
community forums are completed, revisions will be made to the draft, until the final 
draft is completed and presented to the Committee for review and vote. Mr. Stellitano 
confirmed this will be the case, noting that the next forum will be held on September 
16, 2026.  
 
Superintendent Allen noted that a variety of options will be presented and narrowed 
down and the best option will be considered to go forward.  
 
Member Guardiola asked Mr. Stellitano if they were working with the Worcester 
Housing Authority (WHA) to ensure that we are planning adequately for the growth 
being seen in Worcester. Mr. Stellitano noted that his company and the WPS 
administration are working in coordination with the WHA and explained the process of 
accounting for the clearly defined housing projects in development. 
 
Member Guardiola also asked about magnet status and legacy enrollment, to which 
Superintendent Allen discussed the considerations for implementation and logistics to 
be least disruptive to WPS students. Mr. Stellitano noted this will be a Committee 
decision during implementation. 
 
Member Mailman asked questions about magnet programs versus lottery enrollment. 
Jacob Hiatt is the only magnet school with no geographical boundary, per 
Superintendent Allen. Member Maiman asked for a clarification between magnet 
schools and lottery based schools. She noted that parents asked for a clear 
understanding of how students are accepted to certain schools and programs. All 
schools that will not be based on geography will be listed in an upcoming draft. Jacob 
Hiatt will be assigned a neighborhood boundary in the future. 
 
Member Johnson clarified that the Committee should not speak out in favor or oppose 
specific scenarios and the  Committee should remain neutral, taking in all of the 
information and receiving clarification information before they vote in December.
